description: Allow Claude Code's /remote-control channel to authenticate with its own session token instead of the host credential.
Allow sandboxed agents to read the host clipboard for image paste (Ctrl+V).
Tri-state consent for automatic diagnostics bundle upload on error: "" (never asked; prompts and uploads nothing), "yes" (accepted; upload), "no" (declined; never prompt again).
Let an approval of an environment's host commands cover later runs of the same commands, instead of asking each time.

Admit the pinned kit references that replace formerly built-in agents even when kit.allowedSources does not list them, and exempt those references from kit.requireSignature. Credential trust for the fetched content is decided separately, by comparing it against the engine's compiled-in digest. Set to false to require an explicit allowlist entry.
Allow installing kits from local directories or ZIP files. Set to false to require a remote source.
JSON array of allowed kit source prefixes (e.g. ["docker.io/", "ghcr.io/docker/"]). Use ["*"] to allow any remote source.
Verify keyless kit signatures without requiring a Rekor transparency-log entry (for private kits signed with --tlog-upload=false).

Require a valid signature from a trusted signer (kit.trustedSigners) before installing a kit. The pinned kit references that replace formerly built-in agents are exempt while kit.allowExtractedAgents is true.
JSON array of trusted signer policies (key-based {"key":path} or keyless {"issuer":...,"identity":...}). Defaults to Docker employee identities (*@docker.com via https://accounts.google.com).
Force the local MCP gateway even when entitled to the SaaS gateway.

JSON object of inference endpoints for `sbx run --model <model> --provider <id>`, keyed by id, e.g. {"gpubox": {"url": "http://gpubox:8000/v1"}}. Fields: url (required, absolute http(s)), wire ("openai" default or "anthropic"), apiKeyEnv (variable llmman serve reads the API key from), name.
No-proxy exception list for sandbox, daemon, and supported CLI host egress (comma-separated hosts, domain suffixes, and CIDRs).
No-proxy exception list for daemon and supported CLI host egress (overrides no_proxy).
No-proxy exception list for sandbox egress only (overrides no_proxy).
Allow experimental features.

Registry mirror host for Docker Hub-resolving template and kit images (e.g. "artifactory.corp/docker-remote"). A bare host that is not a loopback or wildcard address also mirrors Docker Hub pulls made inside the sandbox, provided the sandbox trusts its certificate. Empty disables mirroring.
Use Docker Hardened Image (DHI) equivalents (dhi/sbx-templates) for agent template images.
Upstream proxy for sandbox, daemon, and supported CLI host egress (URL, PAC source, "system", or "direct"; empty = automatic: HTTP(S)_PROXY if set, otherwise the host OS proxy).
Upstream proxy for daemon and supported CLI host egress (overrides proxy).
Enable integrated NTLM/Kerberos authentication (Windows SSPI) for sandbox, daemon, and supported CLI host egress.
Upstream proxy for sandbox egress only (overrides proxy).

Size of a sandbox's /var/lib/docker volume (minimum 512 MiB; e.g. "10g"). Applies to sandboxes created after the change; existing volumes are never resized. Set DOCKER_SANDBOXES_DOCKER_SIZE to override one sandbox.

Default for an omitted --skills flag or sbx.yaml `skills:` key: "off", "readonly", or "readwrite". Applies to sandboxes created after the change; existing sandboxes' mounts are never retroactively changed.
Allow clients to forward an SSH agent into sandboxes. Existing forwarders require a daemon restart after changes.
Optional fixed host SSH agent socket path. Empty uses each client's current SSH_AUTH_SOCK. Existing forwarders require a daemon restart after changes.
Create a sandbox on SSH connect when it does not exist.
Built-in agent used for SSH auto-created sandboxes.
Template image override for SSH auto-created sandboxes (agent default if empty).
Host directory holding SSH auto-created sandbox workspaces (empty = mount-less, container-internal).
Accept server certificates with a negative serial number (needed by some TLS-inspecting proxies).
